tool.name: EWAS DMR (ML region finder)
tool.description: differentially methylated regions for cross-array longitudinal EWAS, replacing bump hunting
tool.command: mkdir -p in out && ln -s '$mval' in/mval.f64 && ln -s '$dims' in/mval_dims.json && ln -s '$pheno' in/pheno_used.csv && ln -s '$anno' in/probe_annotation.csv && Rscript '$__tool_directory__/../bin/04_dmr_ml.R' --in-dir in --out-dir out --exposure '$design.exposure' --exposure-scale $design.exposure_scale --subject '$design.subject' --covars '$design.covars' --max-gap $cluster.max_gap --rho-min $cluster.rho_min --decay-bp $smooth.decay_bp --lam-grid '$smooth.lam_grid' --cv-folds $smooth.cv_folds --min-probes $call.min_probes --min-effect $call.min_effect --n-perm $infer.n_perm --n-boot $infer.n_boot --seed $infer.seed --var-method '$infer.var_method' #if $infer.also_naive_perm --also-naive-perm #end if

param.name: mval
param.label: Harmonised M-value matrix (mval.f64)
param.help: Column-major float64 dump written by the harmonisation tool.

section.name: cluster
section.title: Co-methylation clustering (replaces the fixed 300 bp gap)

param.name: max_gap
param.label: Maximum genomic gap (bp) considered for joining
param.help: An upper bound only. Two probes within this distance are joined only if they are also co-methylated, so the clusters do not depend on which array panel supplied the probes.

param.name: rho_min
param.label: Minimum within-subject co-methylation to join two probes
param.help: Correlation is computed on subject-demeaned, covariate-adjusted residuals, so it measures co-methylation and not shared between-subject or between-array structure.

param.name: decay_bp
param.label: Distance decay length (bp)
param.help: The fusion penalty between neighbouring probes decays as exp(-d/decay). Large gaps get almost no penalty and are free to break, which is the behaviour a fixed loess span cannot express.

param.name: lam_grid
param.label: Smoothness grid (dimensionless)
param.help: The penalty is scaled by the median precision weight, so this grid transfers across M-values, beta values and cohorts without retuning.

param.name: cv_folds
param.label: Cross-validation folds (over SUBJECTS)
param.help: Whole subjects are held out, never individual visits: splitting a subject's visits would leak the within-subject effect being validated.

param.name: n_perm
param.label: Permutation replicates (within-subject)
param.help: The exposure is permuted only among visits of the same subject, preserving the repeated-measures pairing.

param.name: n_boot
param.label: Stability-selection subsamples
param.help: Fraction of subject subsamples in which a region is re-discovered. Reported alongside the p-value as a robustness score.

param.name: also_naive_perm
param.label: Also run the legacy free permutation
param.help: Runs bumphunter's permutation scheme on the same statistic, so its mis-calibration on this design can be quantified rather than assumed.

tool.help:
**What it does**
Finds differentially methylated regions in a longitudinal EWAS whose samples come from two different Illumina arrays (450K and EPIC). It replaces section 2.6 of the minfi/EWASGalaxy stack -- ``clusterMaker`` with a fixed 300 bp maximum gap, ``loessByCluster`` smoothing with a fixed span, and permutation of the design column of interest.
**Why the original is not valid here**
*Fixed-gap clustering.* Harmonising 450K with EPIC keeps only the probes both arrays carry, which changes the spacing of the panel. On the harmonised set only about half of neighbouring probe pairs fall within 300 bp, so a fixed gap makes a cluster a property of the array panel rather than of the locus.
*Fixed-span loess.* A span defined in probes treats a 50 bp step and a 50 kb step as equally close neighbours, and it returns a smooth curve with no breakpoints, so region boundaries have to be recovered by thresholding.
*Free permutation.* Permuting the exposure across all samples destroys the within-subject pairing. Because subject, cohort, chip and array type are nested in this design, it also creates between-array contrasts that no real reassignment of visit times could produce, so the resulting null is not a null for this design.
**What this tool does instead**
1. within-subject probe-level effects, so the confounded array/cohort/chip terms are absorbed exactly 2. clusters formed only where probes are both close *and* co-methylated 3. weighted total-variation denoising with a distance-decayed penalty -- piecewise-constant output, so breakpoints are explicit, with smoothness chosen by held-out-subject cross-validation 4. family-wise error from within-subject permutation 5. stability selection over subject subsamples 6. cross-array generalisation: every region's effect is re-estimated in the 450K cohort alone and in the EPIC cohort alone and the two are compared
@DESIGN_NOTE@
**Outputs**
The region table carries, per region, the precision-weighted effect in M-value units, its z statistic, the within-subject permutation FWER, the stability score, and the separate 450K and EPIC effect estimates with a direction- concordance flag.
